Both home-manager configs now evaluate cleanly. The NixOS build got past evaluation (it's been running >10 min compiling, not erroring out) — I'll confirm when it lands.

**What happened:** your `flake.lock` bump pulled in a nixpkgs where `nix.settings.experimental-features` became a properly typed option (`list of string`). It used to be part of the freeform `nix.conf` attrset, where the space-separated string `"nix-command flakes"` was accepted verbatim. Now it's type-checked, and a string is rejected.

**Fix** — `[ "nix-command" "flakes" ]` in all three places that set it:

- `nixos/common.nix:19` (the one that failed)
- `home/home.nix:64`
- `home/agent.nix:59`

The last two hadn't errored yet because home-manager's `nix.settings` is still freeform, but they'd have hit the same wall on the next home-manager bump, and the list form renders identically in `nix.conf` either way.

Nothing else in the tree sets that option, so this is the whole change.

Yes — three real gaps. `nix flake update` only re-resolves inputs *you* declare; transitive inputs come from each upstream repo's own lockfile, and that's where things quietly rot.

**1. The whole zellij subtree is frozen, and this is the big one.**

`dim-unfocused` is a `path:` input, so its transitive inputs are governed by `bespoke/zellij/dim-unfocused/flake.lock` — a file in your repo that the top-level update never touches. Result, as of the update you just committed:

| node | locked | tracks |
|---|---|---|
| `nixpkgs_4` (your system) | **2026-09-04** | root input ✅ |
| `nixpkgs` (zellij builds against this) | **2026-08-13** | child lock ❌ |
| `rust-overlay` | **2026-08-15** | child lock ❌ |

Two nodes with the *identical* spec `github:nixos/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable`, three weeks apart. Your zellij and its Rust toolchain are built against August nixpkgs while everything else is on September, and the gap only widens. Closing it means `nix flake update` inside `bespoke/zellij/dim-unfocused` and committing the child lock.

**2. Upstream zellij never arrives on its own.** `zellij-src` tracks `tteggel/zellij@pane-shaders-static` — your fork's branch. The update follows *your branch head*, which only moves when you rebase. Currently `ahead_by=1, behind_by=0` vs `zellij-org:main`, so you're in sync — but only because you did commit `a12494` by hand.

**3. Lockfiles nix doesn't own.** `bespoke/zellij/dim-unfocused/Cargo.lock` (the plugin's Rust deps) needs `cargo update`. And `skillFromNpm` in `home/skills.nix:15` takes a hardcoded version + sha256 — unused today, since your only skill is a flake input, but it's a trap the moment you add one.

**Worth knowing, less urgent:** `nixos-wsl` doesn't `follows` your nixpkgs, so it drags `nixpkgs_3` at **2026-07-11** — pinned by *their* lock, not yours, so your update can't move it. Same shape for `llm-agents` → `nixpkgs_2`. Adding `inputs.nixos-wsl.inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs"` collapses those. Also: the command switches `thixos` only — `yoloixos`, `seed`, and `agent@nix` build from the same lock but are never rebuilt by it.

Everything else checked out — no hard `rev` pins anywhere, no `curl | sh` or `npm -g` escapes, and `nixos-wsl`/`code-review-skill` are at their current branch heads (just quiet repos, not stale).

cat > scripts/update-system.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Bump every lockfile this flake owns, switch to the result, then commit.
#
# `nix flake update` at the top level does NOT recurse into `path:` inputs: a
# path input's transitive deps are read from *that* flake's own flake.lock, so
# the bespoke/zellij/dim-unfocused subtree (zellij-src, rust-overlay, and the
# nixpkgs zellij is built against) silently froze while the rest of the system
# moved on. Update the child lock first, then the top level, so the top-level
# resolve picks up the new subtree.

set -euo pipefail

DOTFILES="$HOME/src/github.com/tteggel/.dotfiles"
CHILD="bespoke/zellij/dim-unfocused"
LOCKS=("flake.lock" "$CHILD/flake.lock")

# Refuse to run over lock edits that aren't committed yet — this script ends in
# a commit of exactly these files, and would otherwise sweep them up.
for lock in "${LOCKS[@]}"; do
  if ! git -C "$DOTFILES" diff --quiet HEAD -- "$lock"; then
    echo "Error: $lock has uncommitted changes" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "==> Updating $CHILD/flake.lock"
nix flake update --flake "$DOTFILES/$CHILD"

echo "==> Updating flake.lock"
nix flake update --flake "$DOTFILES"

echo "==> Switching"
if command -v nixos-rebuild >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake "$DOTFILES#thixos"
else
  home-manager switch --impure --flake "$DOTFILES#thom@nix"
fi

git -C "$DOTFILES" add -- "${LOCKS[@]}"
if git -C "$DOTFILES" diff --cached --quiet -- "${LOCKS[@]}"; then
  echo "==> Inputs already current, nothing to commit"
  exit 0
fi

git -C "$DOTFILES" commit -m 'Update flake inputs'
git -C "$DOTFILES" push
SCRIPT

Done and verified. Two files:

**`scripts/update-system.sh`** (new, executable) — updates `bespoke/zellij/dim-unfocused/flake.lock` *first*, then the top-level lock, then switches, then commits both lockfiles and pushes. Invoked by path from the palette, matching the `gh-sandbox-token.sh` precedent rather than adding a packaged command to both `home.nix` and `agent.nix`.

**`scripts/command-palette.sh:71`** — the inline one-liner is replaced by a call to that script.

Beyond folding in the child update, three things changed versus the old one-liner:

- **The guard covers both lockfiles**, and uses `diff --quiet HEAD` rather than `diff --quiet`, so it catches staged edits too — the old check only saw unstaged ones. Verified it passes on a clean tree and trips on a dirty child lock.
- **"Nothing to commit" is no longer a failure.** The old `&& git commit && git push` chain broke if the inputs were already current, so the push silently never ran and the whole command exited non-zero. It now checks the staged diff and exits 0 with a message.
- Shellcheck-clean.

Two things worth knowing:

1. The palette is packaged via `builtins.readFile`, so the new entry only appears **after** a rebuild. `update-system.sh` runs from the checkout, so it needs no rebuild itself.
2. I restored the lockfiles after testing, so the actual bump isn't taken yet — the commit is purely tooling. Running "Update system" (after a rebuild) will apply it: zellij's nixpkgs `08-13 → 09-04`, rust-overlay `08-15 → 09-05`, plus whatever `llm-agents` has moved to since.

This doesn't touch gap #2 from before — the zellij fork still only advances when you rebase `pane-shaders-static` by hand.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Bump every lockfile this flake owns, switch to the result, then commit.
#
# `nix flake update` at the top level does NOT recurse into `path:` inputs: a
# path input's transitive deps are read from *that* flake's own flake.lock, so
# the bespoke/zellij/dim-unfocused subtree (zellij-src, rust-overlay, and the
# nixpkgs zellij is built against) silently froze while the rest of the system
# moved on. Update the child lock first, then the top level, so the top-level
# resolve picks up the new subtree.

set -euo pipefail

DOTFILES="$HOME/src/github.com/tteggel/.dotfiles"
CHILD="bespoke/zellij/dim-unfocused"
LOCKS=("flake.lock" "$CHILD/flake.lock")

# Refuse to run over lock edits that aren't committed yet — this script ends in
# a commit of exactly these files, and would otherwise sweep them up.
for lock in "${LOCKS[@]}"; do
  if ! git -C "$DOTFILES" diff --quiet HEAD -- "$lock"; then
    echo "Error: $lock has uncommitted changes" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "==> Updating $CHILD/flake.lock"
nix flake update --flake "$DOTFILES/$CHILD"

echo "==> Updating flake.lock"
nix flake update --flake "$DOTFILES"

echo "==> Switching"
if command -v nixos-rebuild >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake "$DOTFILES#thixos"
else
  home-manager switch --impure --flake "$DOTFILES#thom@nix"
fi

git -C "$DOTFILES" add -- "${LOCKS[@]}"
if git -C "$DOTFILES" diff --cached --quiet -- "${LOCKS[@]}"; then
  echo "==> Inputs already current, nothing to commit"
  exit 0
fi

git -C "$DOTFILES" commit -m 'Update flake inputs'
git -C "$DOTFILES" push
